To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) LBP and LTP based features are very effective for face recognition; 2)LTPs and distance transform based matching improve LBP based features; 3) combining LBP/LTP with Gabor wavelet features and Kernel PCA improves performance; 4) the combination of these techniques with illumination normalization improves robustness to changing lighting conditions; and 5) the resulting system provides state-of-the art performance for face recognition under uncontrolled illumination.

the combination of illumination normalization, local ternary patterns, distance transform-based similarity measures, kernel-based feature sets, and multiple feature fusion is a powerful and effective approach that provides state-of-the art performance for face recognition under difficult lighting conditions.

1) distance transform based matching improves the performance of local texture-based face descriptors, and 2) combining the distance transform with kernel-based feature extraction, Gabor wavelets and the local ternary pattern yields state-of-the-art face recognition performance under difficult illumination conditions.
